prompt: Hybridization and shape of carbon in the methyl carbocation CH₃⁺?
explain: CH₃⁺ has 3 σ bonds and an empty p orbital, so it is sp² and planar.

prompt: Hybridization and shape of the methyl carbanion CH₃⁻?
explain: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair gives sp³, pyramidal like NH₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Percentage s-character in an sp² hybrid orbital?
explain: sp² = one s + two p orbitals, so s-character is 1/3.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of C–C bond length among ethane, ethene and ethyne?
explain: Bond length is 154 pm, 134 pm and 120 pm; more bond order means shorter.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of π bonds in propyne, CH₃–C≡CH?
explain: A triple bond has 1 σ and 2 π bonds; the CH₃ group adds none.

prompt: In allene, CH₂=C=CH₂, the central carbon is hybridized as:

prompt: Hybridization of carbon and nitrogen in CH₃–C≡N (nitrile group)?
explain: Each atom of the C≡N triple bond has 2 σ-region pairs, so both are sp.

prompt: Which carbon–hydrogen bond is the shortest?

prompt: Hybridization of the carbonyl carbon in acetone, (CH₃)₂C=O?
explain: It has three σ bonds and one π bond, so it is sp² and trigonal planar.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hybridization of carbon atoms in graphite and in diamond respectively?
explain: Graphite has planar layers (sp²); diamond has a tetrahedral network (sp³).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is HC≡CH more acidic than CH₂=CH₂ and CH₃–CH₃?
options: sp carbon has the highest s-character
It has the most σ bonds
It has the most H atoms

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of π bonds in acrylonitrile, CH₂=CH–C≡N?
explain: One π bond in C=C and two in C≡N gives 3.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electronic configuration of carbon in the excited state that explains its tetravalency?
explain: One 2s electron is promoted to 2p, giving 4 unpaired electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbon-centred species is most stable by hybridization effect?
explain: Carbanion stability rises with s-character: sp > sp² > sp³.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Shape and C–C–C angle around each carbon of benzene?
explain: All six carbons are sp² in a planar hexagon with 120° angles.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Highest priority as principal functional group in IUPAC naming?
explain: Order: acid > anhydride > ester > acyl halide > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group is always cited only as a prefix in IUPAC names?
explain: Nitro (like halo, alkoxy) is never a suffix; –CN, –NH₂, –CHO can be suffixes.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Propanoic acid and methyl ethanoate are which type of isomers?
explain: Acid (–COOH) and ester (–COOR) share CₙH₂ₙO₂ but have different functional groups.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A functional isomer of but-1-yne (C₄H₆) is:
explain: Alkynes and alkadienes share CₙH₂ₙ₋₂; they differ in functional group.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Alkenes and cycloalkanes are examples of which isomerism?
explain: Same CₙH₂ₙ, one open-chain and the other cyclic: ring-chain isomerism.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which one is a non-benzenoid aromatic compound?
explain: Azulene (5+7 fused rings, 10 π e⁻) is aromatic without a benzene ring.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these is an alicyclic compound?
explain: Alicyclic = carbocyclic, non-aromatic. Pyridine and furan are heterocyclic aromatic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of primary (1°) hydrogens in isobutane (2-methylpropane)?
explain: Three CH₃ groups give 9 primary H; the one on central C is tertiary.

prompt: Hybridisation of carbon in the nitrile group –C≡N?
explain: Carbon with one triple bond and one single bond has two σ bonds, so it is sp.

prompt: Successive members of a homologous series differ by:
explain: A –CH₂– unit (14 u) separates successive homologues with the same functional group.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Homolytic fission is most favoured under which conditions?
options: UV light or heat, non-polar medium

subject: Chemistry

prompt: In heterolysis of a C–Z bond, a carbanion forms when Z is:
options: More electronegative than C, e.g. Cl
Less electronegative than C, e.g. Li

subject: Chemistry

prompt: In mechanism arrows, a single-barbed (fishhook) arrow shows movement of:
options: A lone pair to form a π bond
explain: The half-headed (fishhook) arrow shows one-electron movement in homolysis. The full-headed arrow shows a pair moving.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which magnetic property do free radicals formed by homolysis show?
explain: Free radicals contain an unpaired electron, so they are paramagnetic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which bond in an organic peroxide such as benzoyl peroxide breaks homolytically on heating?
explain: The weak O–O bond cleaves homolytically to give RO• radicals, which act as radical initiators.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In heterolysis of the C–Cl bond in CH₃–Cl, the shared electron pair goes to:

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Homolytic fission of a covalent bond A–B gives species with how many electrons in the broken bond's share?
options: One unpaired electron on each fragment
A pair of electrons on A only
A pair of electrons on B only
explain: Homolysis splits the bonding pair equally, so each fragment gets one electron, giving two radicals.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these is an ambident nucleophile?
explain: CN⁻ can attack through C or N (two nucleophilic sites); Cl⁻, OH⁻ and NH₂⁻ have one donor atom.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Carbene :CH₂ behaves as an electrophile because its carbon has:
explain: Carbon in a carbene has only 6 valence electrons, so it can accept an electron pair.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Nucleophilicity order of oxygen nucleophiles (strongest first):
explain: For the same attacking atom, nucleophilicity follows basicity: CH₃O⁻ > OH⁻ > CH₃COO⁻.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In polar protic solvents, nucleophilicity of halides is:

prompt: In polar aprotic solvents (DMSO, DMF), halide nucleophilicity order is:

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of nucleophilic strength across the second period:
explain: Nucleophilicity falls as electronegativity rises across a period: NH₂⁻ > OH⁻ > F⁻.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these cannot act as a nucleophile?
explain: NH₄⁺ has no lone pair on N, so it cannot donate an electron pair.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electrophile in Friedel–Crafts acylation (RCOCl + AlCl₃):
explain: AlCl₃ abstracts Cl⁻ from RCOCl to give the acylium ion RC≡O⁺.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Attacking electrophile in the Reimer–Tiemann reaction:
explain: CHCl₃ with a base gives CCl₃⁻, which loses Cl⁻ to form electrophilic :CCl₂.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: tert-Butoxide ion is a strong base but a poor nucleophile because of:
explain: The bulky (CH₃)₃C– group hinders attack on carbon, so it mostly abstracts H⁺ (elimination).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which one is a neutral electrophile?
explain: SO₃ is neutral but electron-deficient at sulfur, so it attacks benzene in sulfonation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The electrophile in the azo-coupling of phenol is:
explain: The diazonium cation is a weak electrophile that attacks the activated para position of phenol.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Inductive effect weakens with distance and becomes negligible after about how many carbon atoms?
explain: The effect falls off rapidly along a σ-chain and is almost negligible beyond the third carbon.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Strongest acid among CH₃COOH, ClCH₂COOH, Cl₂CHCOOH, Cl₃CCOOH?
explain: Three Cl atoms give the largest total –I effect, which stabilises the carboxylate ion most.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Inductive effect of a group is measured relative to which reference atom?
explain: Groups that attract electrons more than H show –I. Groups that release them show +I.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of –I effect based on the hybridisation of carbon:
explain: Greater s-character means higher electronegativity, so –C≡CH > –CH=CH₂ > –CH₂CH₃ in –I.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–Cl, which carbon carries the largest partial positive charge?
explain: The –I effect of Cl is strongest at the adjacent carbon and decreases along the chain.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group shows a +I effect?
explain: Negatively charged groups such as –COO⁻ and –O⁻ release electrons (+I). –NH₃⁺, –NO₂ and –CN show –I.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these groups has the strongest –I effect?
explain: The –I order is –NO₂ > –F > –OH > –OCH₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Inductive effect is best described as which type of electron displacement?
explain: It is a permanent polarisation of σ-bonds. Electromeric effect is the temporary one, and it involves π-bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Gas-phase basicity of methylamines, where +I effect dominates:
explain: Without solvation, the +I effect of more alkyl groups raises electron density on N.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of stability of carbanions arising from +I effect of alkyl groups:
explain: +I groups intensify the negative charge, so more alkyl substitution destabilises the carbanion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In water, the order of acidity of alcohols is influenced by +I effect as:
explain: Alkyl groups push electrons onto O, which destabilises RO⁻, so more alkyl substitution lowers acidity.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is the stronger acid because of the +I effect of the alkyl group in the other?
explain: Alkyl groups donate electrons (+I) and destabilise the carboxylate, so HCOOH, with no alkyl group, is the strongest.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of –I effect among –F, –OH, –NH₂ across the second period:
explain: –I strength follows electronegativity of the attached atom: F > O > N.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the gas phase, which amine is the weakest base due to the –I effect of fluorine?
explain: The –I effect of CF₃ withdraws electron density from N and lowers its availability for protonation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In CH₃–CH=CH₂ with H⁺, the π pair shifts to which carbon?
explain: +E: π pair goes to the carbon that bonds H⁺, giving the more stable 2° carbocation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the electromeric effect, the shared π pair is:
options: Shared with an adjacent σ bond
explain: E effect is a complete transfer of the π electron pair to one atom, unlike polarisation in I effect.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Addition of CN⁻ to CH₂=CH–CHO shows which standard classification of E effect?
options: No E effect, as C=C is present
explain: A nucleophile attacking carbon makes the π pair shift away from it: –E.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these compounds can show the electromeric effect?
explain: Electromeric effect needs a multiple bond (π electrons); saturated molecules lack it.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the +E effect, the π pair is shifted toward the atom that:
options: Is always the more electronegative atom
Is the carbon of the π bond
explain: +E: π electrons move to the atom that becomes bonded to the attacking reagent (e.g. electrophile).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: If inductive and electromeric effects oppose each other during a reaction, which dominates?
explain: The electromeric effect, being a complete π shift, overrides the inductive effect.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: On removal of the attacking reagent, the polarised multiple bond shows what change in electromeric effect?
options: Reverts to the original unpolarised state
explain: Electromeric effect exists only in the presence of the attacking reagent; the π pair returns once the reagent is removed.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Resonance energy of a molecule is the difference between its energy and that of the:
options: Resonance hybrid, in the opposite sense
explain: Resonance energy = energy of most stable contributing structure minus energy of the actual hybrid.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Resonance hybrid is ____ stable than any of its contributing structures.
explain: Delocalisation lowers energy; hybrid is more stable than every canonical form.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which halogen shows the weakest +M effect due to poor p-orbital overlap with carbon 2p?
explain: Larger 5p orbital of I overlaps poorly with C 2p, so +M is weakest.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Halogens on benzene are o/p directing but ring deactivating because:
explain: –I deactivates the ring; +M enriches o/p positions, so directing is o/p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbocation is most stabilised by resonance?
explain: Benzyl cation's positive charge is delocalised over the ring; the others only have inductive/hyperconjugation stabilisation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is a –M group?
explain: –CN withdraws π electrons by resonance (–M); –Cl and –NHCOCH₃ are +M, –CH₃ is hyperconjugating.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Mesomeric effect operates through which type of bonds/electrons?
explain: The mesomeric effect is the transmission of π electrons or lone pairs in a conjugated system.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol mainly because:
explain: The negative charge of phenoxide delocalises into the ring; ethoxide has none.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Aniline is a weaker base than methylamine mainly due to:
explain: N lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring, making it less available for protonation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of equivalent major resonance structures drawn (Kekulé type) for the carboxylate ion RCOO⁻:
explain: Two equivalent forms with the negative charge on either oxygen; C–O bond order is 1.5.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is the most stable resonance contributor rule among these?
explain: Octet-complete structures, more covalent bonds and minimal charge separation are more stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In –M effect, the substituent attached to the conjugated system:
options: Has no effect on π cloud
explain: –M groups such as –NO₂, –CHO, –CN pull π electrons toward themselves, lowering ring density at o/p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hyperconjugation is also known as:
explain: Delocalisation of σ(C–H) electrons gives structures with no C–H bond, so it is called no-bond resonance.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Baker–Nathan order of hyperconjugative effect of alkyl groups is:
explain: The number of α-H decreases from CH₃ (3) to t-Bu (0), so the order is Me > Et > i-Pr > t-Bu.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of hyperconjugative structures of ethyl carbocation, CH₃CH₂⁺?
explain: Only the CH₃ carbon is α to C⁺ and it has 3 α-H, so 3 structures.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of hyperconjugative structures of isopropyl cation, (CH₃)₂CH⁺?
explain: Two CH₃ groups attached to C⁺ give 2 × 3 = 6 α-H, so 6 structures.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of α-hydrogens in 2-methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃?
explain: Two CH₃ on C2 (6 H) plus the CH₃ on C3 (3 H) give 9 α-H.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which alkene cannot show hyperconjugation?
explain: In CH₂=CH–C(CH₃)₃ the carbon attached to the sp² carbon is quaternary and has no α-H.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Lowest heat of hydrogenation is shown by:
explain: It has 12 α-H, the most hyperconjugation, so it is the most stable and releases the least heat.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbocation gets NO stabilisation by hyperconjugation?
explain: CH₃⁺ has no α-carbon and so no α-H to overlap with the empty p orbital.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Preference for the more substituted alkene (Saytzeff rule) is explained mainly by:
explain: More alkyl groups on C=C give more α-H and more hyperconjugation, so the alkene is more stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In propene, the C(sp³)–C(sp²) bond is shorter than a normal C–C single bond because of:
explain: No-bond structures (H⁺ CH₂=CH–CH₂⁻) give the C–C bond partial double-bond character.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hyperconjugation is best described as a:
explain: σ(C–H) electrons delocalise into an adjacent π or p system, and the effect is permanent.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of stability of alkyl free radicals due to hyperconjugation:
explain: More α-H give more hyperconjugative structures, so 3° > 2° > 1° > ·CH₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the canonical form H⁺ CH₂=CH–CH₂⁻ of propene, the C–H bond that is broken is:
explain: Only the σ(C–H) bond of the CH₃ attached to the sp² carbon takes part in hyperconjugation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of α-H taking part in hyperconjugation of ethylbenzene (C₆H₅CH₂CH₃)?
explain: Only the benzylic CH₂ is attached to the ring, so 2 α-H; the CH₃ is not α.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Trans-2-butene is more stable than 1-butene mainly because it has:

subject: Chemistry

prompt: The C–H bond that is involved in hyperconjugation becomes slightly:
explain: σ(C–H) electron density is partly delocalised, so that bond is slightly longer and weaker.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hybridisation of the positively charged carbon in a carbocation is:
explain: Three σ bonds, trigonal planar, with an empty p orbital: sp².
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Driving force for a 1,2-hydride or 1,2-methyl shift in a carbocation:
options: Formation of a more stable carbocation
Increase in the number of σ bonds
explain: Shift occurs to give an equally or more stable carbocation (2°→3°).

prompt: Neopentyl cation (CH₃)₃C–CH₂⁺ rearranges mainly by:
options: Loss of H⁺ to give an alkyne
explain: No β-H exists; CH₃ shift gives the 3° tert-amyl cation (CH₃)₂C⁺–CH₂CH₃.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is the most stable carbocation?
explain: Allyl cation is resonance stabilised; vinyl and methyl cations are least stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Vinyl cation CH₂=CH⁺ compared with ethyl cation CH₃CH₂⁺ is:
options: More stable, due to sp carbon
Less stable, due to sp carbon
explain: The sp carbon is more electronegative and holds the positive charge poorly; no hyperconjugation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of hyperconjugative structures of (CH₃)₃C⁺ (tert-butyl cation):
explain: Nine α C–H bonds give nine hyperconjugative structures.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of stability: Ph₃C⁺, Ph₂CH⁺, PhCH₂⁺
explain: More phenyl groups give more delocalisation of the positive charge.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbocation is aromatic and exceptionally stable?
explain: Tropylium ion is planar, cyclic, with 6 π electrons (Hückel rule).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is more stable: CH₃OCH₂⁺ or CH₃CH₂⁺?
explain: The oxygen lone pair back-donates, giving CH₃–O⁺=CH₂ with complete octets.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A carbocation intermediate in SN1 on a chiral centre gives mainly:
explain: The planar cation is attacked from both faces by the nucleophile.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Main product of CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + benzene with AlCl₃ is:
explain: The 1° propyl cation rearranges by a 1,2-H shift to the 2° isopropyl cation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: HCl adds to 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene. Major product is:
explain: The 2° cation undergoes a CH₃ shift to the 3° cation, which is then trapped by Cl⁻.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Acid dehydration of 3-methylbutan-2-ol gives major alkene:
explain: 2° cation shifts H to give the 3° cation; Saytzeff elimination gives 2-methylbut-2-ene.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Cyclobutylmethyl cation rearranges to cyclopentyl cation because of:
explain: Alkyl shift expands the strained 4-ring to a 5-ring and gives a 1°→2° cation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Rearrangement of a 1,2-shift in carbocations is generally NOT favoured when it gives:
options: A less stable cation from a more stable one
explain: Shifts go downhill in energy; 3°→2° is uphill and not favoured.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is a bridgehead carbocation in a small bicyclic system (e.g. norbornyl) very unstable?
explain: The ring forces a pyramidal geometry, preventing sp² planarity and stabilisation.

prompt: Number of resonance structures of benzyl cation (including the CH₂⁺ one):
explain: Charge on benzylic C plus ortho, ortho and para ring carbons: 4 structures.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hyperconjugation in carbocations is also called:
explain: α C–H σ electrons overlap with the empty p orbital; this is also known as the Baker–Nathan effect.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which group attached to a carbocation centre destabilises it most?
explain: –NO₂ withdraws electrons by –I and –M, intensifying the positive charge.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Carbocation rearrangement by 1,2-alkyl or hydride shift is commonly called the ___ rearrangement.
explain: 1,2-shifts of H or alkyl in carbocations are Wagner–Meerwein rearrangements.

prompt: Cyclopentadienyl cation (C₅H₅⁺) is best described as:
explain: It is planar and cyclic with 4π electrons (4n), so it is antiaromatic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Most stable among the benzyl cations with the para substituent shown:
explain: The +M effect of –OCH₃ delocalises the positive charge; –NO₂ withdraws electrons and destabilises it.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Isobutyl cation (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂⁺ rearranges quickly to:
explain: A 1,2-hydride shift converts the 1° cation into the 3° tert-butyl cation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Among simple alkyl carbanions, which is the most stable?
explain: +I groups intensify negative charge, so stability is CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3°, the reverse of carbocations.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Geometry and hybridisation of carbon in a simple alkyl free radical:
explain: The alkyl radical carbon is sp² with the unpaired electron in a p orbital (planar or nearly so).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which radical is the most stable?
explain: Ph₃C• (trityl) delocalises the unpaired electron over three phenyl rings, giving the most resonance.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: An electron-withdrawing (–I) group attached to the carbanion carbon does what?
explain: –I and –M groups delocalise or disperse the negative charge, which stabilises the carbanion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is the cyclopentadienyl anion unusually stable?
explain: The cyclic planar anion has 6π electrons, which satisfy Hückel's rule (4n+2) and make it aromatic.

prompt: The cyclopropenyl anion is unstable because it is:
explain: Cyclic planar with 4π electrons, 4n type, so it is antiaromatic and destabilised.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbanion is most stable?
explain: The charge is delocalised onto oxygen by the –M effect of NO₂, so this carbanion is resonance stabilised.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Chief reason for the stability order of alkyl radicals 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃•:
explain: More α C–H bonds give more hyperconjugation, which stabilises the electron-deficient radical.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: How many electrons are in the valence shell of carbon in a methyl free radical?
explain: CH₃• has three bond pairs (6 e⁻) and one unpaired electron, so 7. A carbanion has 8 and a carbocation 6.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Free radicals are generally:
explain: The unpaired electron makes free radicals paramagnetic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Among CH₃⁻, NH₂⁻, OH⁻ and F⁻, the most stable anion is:
explain: Across a period, the more electronegative atom holds the negative charge better, so F⁻ is most stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The carbon bonded to Mg in a Grignard reagent R–MgX behaves as a:
explain: The C–Mg bond is polarised toward carbon, so R behaves as R⁻ (a carbanion nucleophile).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Relative stability of carbanions: which order is correct for CH₃⁻, CH₂=CH⁻, HC≡C⁻ ?
explain: s-character: sp (50%) > sp² (33%) > sp³ (25%); more s-character stabilises the carbanion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbanion is most stable due to resonance with the ring (delocalisation)?
explain: Benzyl carbanion's negative charge delocalises into the benzene ring; alkyl groups (+I) destabilise carbanions.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon gives product with which stereochemical outcome?
explain: Backside attack by the nucleophile inverts configuration (Walden inversion) in SN2.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Optically active alkyl halide reacting by SN1 mainly gives product that is:
explain: The planar carbocation is attacked from both faces, giving racemisation, with slight excess of inversion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Rate of SN2 for alkyl halides follows the order:
explain: SN2 is governed by steric hindrance at the carbon, so the least hindered CH₃X reacts fastest.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Saytzeff (Zaitsev) rule predicts the major product of β-elimination to be the:
explain: Saytzeff: the more stable, more highly substituted alkene predominates.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: E2 elimination proceeds most readily when H and leaving group are:
explain: E2 is a concerted anti elimination requiring an anti-periplanar H and leaving group.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Polar protic solvents (like H₂O, ROH) favour which pathway for alkyl halides?
explain: Protic solvents stabilise the carbocation and the leaving group, favouring SN1; polar aprotic solvents favour SN2.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hofmann elimination of quaternary ammonium hydroxide gives mainly:
explain: The bulky NR₃ leaving group removes the most accessible (least hindered) β-H, giving the Hofmann product.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of the following is a nucleophile but not an anion?

subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these is a neutral nucleophile?
explain: R₃N has a lone pair on N, so it donates electrons; the other three are electron-deficient electrophiles.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon of C=O. The electromeric shift gives which species?
explain: The π pair moves fully to the more electronegative O, which gives R₂C(Nu)–O⁻, an alkoxide.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which pair of conditions is needed for the electromeric effect to operate?
options: Multiple bond and an attacking reagent
Single bond and a polar solvent
Lone pair on an adjacent atom only
explain: The effect needs a π bond (multiple bond) and is induced only when an attacking reagent approaches.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Cyclopropylmethyl cation is unusually stable mainly because of:
options: Overlap of bent C–C bonds with empty p orbital
Relief of angle strain by ring opening
explain: Bent (banana) σ bonds of cyclopropane conjugate with the empty p orbital, delocalising the charge.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Friedel–Crafts acylation gives no rearranged product because the acylium ion R–C≡O⁺ is:
options: Resonance stabilised with octet on all atoms
A primary carbocation that never shifts
Quickly converted to a tertiary cation
explain: R–C⁺=O ↔ R–C≡O⁺ gives an octet on every atom, so no 1,2-shift occurs.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of stability of simple alkyl carbanions (+I effect destabilises):
explain: +I groups intensify negative charge on carbon, so stability falls CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3°.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which carbanion is least stable?
explain: Three +I methyl groups concentrate charge on carbon, making the 3° carbanion least stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which radical is more stable than the others?
explain: Benzyl radical is resonance stabilised over the ring; this outweighs hyperconjugation in alkyl radicals.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Nitrating mixture (conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄) generates which attacking electrophile on benzene?
explain: H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃, which loses water to give the nitronium ion NO₂⁺, the electrophile.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of the following is an electrophile that has a vacant orbital and carries a positive charge?
explain: A carbocation has an empty p orbital (sextet carbon), so it accepts an electron pair and is an electrophile.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In ethene, the C=C π bond arises from which overlap?
options: Sidewise overlap of unhybridised p orbitals
Head-on overlap of two p orbitals
Sidewise overlap of sp² hybrid orbitals
explain: The σ bond is sp²–sp² head-on. The π bond is the lateral overlap of the unhybridised 2p orbitals.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Shape of ethyne and its H–C≡C bond angle?
explain: Each carbon is sp hybridised, so the sp orbitals lie 180° apart and the molecule is linear.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electrophile generated from CO + HCl with AlCl₃ in the Gattermann–Koch reaction is:
explain: CO + HCl + AlCl₃ gives the formyl cation HCO⁺, which formylates benzene to benzaldehyde.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Alkyl halide + AgCN (covalent cyanide) mainly gives which product type?
explain: Ag–C bond is covalent, so only the N lone pair is free to attack; CN⁻ is ambident and AgCN gives R–NC.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, the weak electrophile attacked by phenoxide ion is:
explain: The carbon of CO₂ is electron-deficient (δ+), so the phenoxide ring attacks it to give salicylic acid.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which pair correctly shows the electromeric effect for H⁺ adding to C=O in an aldehyde?
options: π pair moves to oxygen, which takes H⁺ (+E)
π pair moves to carbon, which takes H⁺ (+E)
No shift occurs without a nucleophile
explain: The electrophile H⁺ bonds to O; the π pair shifts to O (+E), leaving C⁺.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electromeric effect differs from the mesomeric effect in being:
options: Dynamic, shown only during reagent attack
Permanent, present in the ground state
explain: Mesomeric effect is a permanent ground-state effect; electromeric is a dynamic effect that appears only at the attack stage.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: n-Propyl cation CH₃CH₂CH₂⁺ rearranges to isopropyl cation through a:
explain: H moves with its bonding pair from C2 to C1, converting a 1° cation into a more stable 2° cation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In a 1,2-hydride shift in a carbocation, the migrating hydrogen moves with:
options: An electron pair from the empty p orbital
explain: The H migrates as hydride, carrying the C–H bonding pair to the adjacent cationic carbon.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these cations is aromatic?
explain: C₃H₃⁺ is cyclic, planar and fully conjugated with 2 π electrons, which fits 4n+2 (n = 0).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In acid-catalysed hydration of an alkene, the slow (rate-determining) step is formation of:
options: A carbocation by protonation of the C=C
explain: H⁺ adds to the π bond to give a carbocation slowly. Water then attacks it quickly.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which radical is more stable?
explain: Allyl radical is resonance-stabilised, which beats the hyperconjugation in 3° alkyl radicals.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Most stable carbanion among the following:
explain: Charge in Ph₃C⁻ is delocalised over three phenyl rings, so it is the most stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which hydrocarbon is the most acidic?
explain: Its conjugate base, the cyclopentadienyl anion, is aromatic (6π e⁻), so pKa is about 16.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of electrons in the valence shell of carbon in the methyl carbanion CH₃⁻:
explain: 3 bond pairs plus 1 lone pair give an octet of 8 electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The lone pair of the phenyl carbanion C₆H₅⁻ is located in:
options: A p orbital conjugated with the ring
An sp² orbital in the ring plane
An sp³ orbital above the ring
An sp orbital along the axis
explain: The lone pair lies in the ring plane, perpendicular to the π system, so it is not delocalised.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In allylic bromination of propene with NBS, Br• abstracts H from:
explain: Allylic H abstraction gives the resonance-stabilised allyl radical.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Compared with the ethyl radical, the vinyl radical CH₂=CH• is:
options: More stable, as it has sp² carbon
explain: The unpaired electron sits in an sp² σ orbital with no delocalisation, so vinyl is less stable.
